messages:
sam: hi team, new hire here. trying to compile runtime from source inside our dev container and the compile fails when invoking nvcc: `ptxas: command not found`. build log snippet:
```
/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas: not found
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
I have CUDA toolkit installed on host, and in container /usr/local/cuda exists but no ptxas. anyone seen this? who owns the base images?

ryan_rt: welcome! two quick things: 1) ensure the image includes the CUDA toolkit dev package, not just the runtime (libcudart). ptxas is part of cuda-toolkit/bin. 2) We usually mount /usr/local/cuda from host in dev containers; check your dockerfile or docker run flags. Are you using multi-stage build that strips toolchain out?

maria_infra: infra note: dev boxes use host-driver + toolkit; base image should be `nvidia/cuda:11.8-devel-ubuntu22.04` for builds. If you're using `-base` or `-runtime` images, they lack ptxas. If you need GPU compile in container, use `-devel` or install `cuda-toolkit-11-8` in the image. Also confirm `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `nvidia-container-toolkit` aren't masking /usr/local/cuda.

sam: ah makes sense — I mistakenly used `nvidia/cuda:11.8-base` in the dockerfile. switching to `-devel` fixed ptxas presence and the build progressed further. thanks! I'll open a tiny PR to update the onboarding guide to recommend `-devel` for build-from-source steps.

dev-bot: ci/checklist: Remember to run local smoke `make smoke` inside the devel image so nvcc-related tests pass before pushing the PR.

sam: will do, thanks everyone :party_popper:
